idiom_name: node classes or Struct subclasses with named readers + case dispatch
implementation_notes: Ruby is dynamically typed, so the pattern is realised with plain classes exposing named readers, or with Struct.new(:left, :op, :right), which generates the constructor and the named accessors and checks member arity at construction. Dispatch is a case expression over node classes or a method per class, and Data.define (Ruby 3.2) gives the same named readers with immutability when nodes must not change after construction. Keep named fields while node shapes differ; if generic traversal is needed, expose a children array derived from Struct#members or an explicit method.
code_sketch:
Binary = Struct.new(:left, :op, :right)   # named accessors, arity checked at construction

def print_node(node)
  case node
  when Binary then "(#{print_node(node.left)} #{node.op} #{print_node(node.right)})"
  when Integer then node.to_s
  else raise ArgumentError, "unhandled node: #{node.class}"
  end
end
pitfalls: Struct members are positional and mutable: the constructor argument order is an untyped contract and any reader can be reassigned later.
case/when has no exhaustiveness, so an unhandled node class falls through unless every dispatch site ends in else raise.
Method lookup on every node visit makes per-node dispatch slower than a table would be, which matters in hot analysis loops.
